repairFindingHistory.observedClaim: The first repaired version said every shrine younger than five seconds healed exactly the minimum, despite progressive growth and an unknown intermediate formula.

evidence.quote: restores at least (25/50/75/100/125 + (40% Ability Power)) Health to the first ally to enter.
성소의 체력 회복 효과는 점차 증가해, 5초 이후에는 최대 (50/87.5/125/162.5/200 + (70% 주문력))의 체력을 회복시킬 수 있습니다.

repairFindingHistory.verifiedFinalCorrection: The final heal rule states growth above the minimum and the larger amount after five seconds, preserves min/max as bounds, and keeps intermediate interpolation unresolved. No exact immature plateau remains.

repairFindingHistory.observedClaim: The repaired per-100 ratio incorrectly assigned the movement-speed output to caster.

evidence.quote: Health to the first ally to enter.

repairFindingHistory.verifiedFinalCorrection: ratio_output moveSpeed now belongs to ally; ratio_input abilityPower belongs to caster.

repairFindingHistory.observedClaim: Self shield/speed rules were unconditional on cast, granting self effects even on an allied-recipient cast.

evidence.quote: Grants Annie or an ally a shield, a burst of Move Speed

repairFindingHistory.verifiedFinalCorrection: Other-allied-champion and self-selected recipients are explicitly mutually exclusive. Both shield and speed branches use the same recipient selection, while the independent Tibbers clause remains separate.

notes.detail: All 15 repaired candidates were read again. All 15 input file hashes are unchanged from the initial complete English/Korean source reading. Newly introduced text, conditions, source-number references and owner fields were checked. Three further repair errors were reported to root and their updated final files were re-read before this report.
Sun Disc AP owner is now unknown with a matching scope gap. Unspecified damage recipient/event are not filled from external game knowledge.
The tooltip's non-primary-target percentage endpoints are preserved; exact intermediate values are explicitly unknown. The primary attack target relation is no longer declared unknowable.

English gives the out-of-combat movement buff a 20-second duration; Korean wording sounds like a 20-second out-of-combat prerequisite. The final candidate follows English and records both excerpts as source_conflict. Unknown experience/Meep period/cap/Chime thresholds are still gaps.

Second distinct enemy and wall collision are explicit text conditions because dedicated second-target/wall enums do not exist. The text correctly limits stun to enemies already hit; a generic nearby_enemies subject does not claim a new AoE stun.

Intermediate shrine growth cannot be calculated from the supplied source. The final text/gap now preserve the minimum as a lower bound and larger mature endpoint, without a flat immature amount or an invented interpolation curve. Endpoint AP coefficients are retained as formula components.
The one in one-way is excluded from numeric parameters, and direction remains in text. No exact portal distance was invented.

The source describes four ability uses and the next damaging ability, but does not fully specify counter reset or multi-target consumption sequencing. This review does not add hidden proc/counter algorithms absent from the source.
The self recipient is now selected conditionally. The current-shield/enemy retaliation limit is preserved as text rather than a false count parameter; unknown internal state storage is not invented.

Three English enrage causes and recast orders are preserved. The pooled unknown Tibbers stat block retains exact evidence and an unsupported_formula gap; it does not assert a resolved fabricated stat equation. The Korean omission of summon enrage is source asymmetry rather than an explicit denial.

No concrete remaining source disagreement was found in these snapshots. This is not a blanket assertion of all hidden gameplay behavior and does not grant final approval; root remains responsible for ledger/approval decisions.

initialReview.scope: All P/Q/W/E/R slots of Azir, Bard, Annie. Supplied sources and source-number references only; no external gameplay facts, no candidate/code/schema changes.
criteria: ordinary effects must not inherit special-result conditions
optional permission must not become a prerequisite
special-target effects must not become universal
casts/stacks/entities are not target hit counts
maturity/expiry timers are not automatic heal or damage durations
English priority and meaningful locale disagreements

failures.claim: The AP coefficient is assigned to summon, although the supplied source never identifies Sun Disc AP as the input stat.

evidence.quote: The Sun Disc deals ((230 ~ 410) + (40% Ability Power)) magic damage

failures.correction: Do not assert summon AP. Use caster only if the extraction convention establishes caster-owned tooltip coefficients; otherwise use unknown and add a scope_ambiguous gap. This review does not infer the owner from outside game knowledge.

failures.claim: Both normal damage and slow require hit_count = 75. en:body:n0 is the first base-damage value, not a hit threshold.

evidence.quote: dealing (75/95/115/135/155 + (35/40/45/50/55% Ability Power)) magic damage to enemies they pass through and Slowing them by 25% for 1 second.

failures.correction: Remove the invented hit_count condition. Apply damage and slow to enemies the soldiers pass through; preserve no extra damage from multiple soldiers separately or in explicit text.

failures.claim: On-hit application is incorrectly limited to champion targets.

evidence.quote: Sand Soldiers apply On-hits at 50% damage once per attack to Azir's primary target.

failures.correction: Require the primary attack target and a soldier attack, without inventing a champion-only restriction.

failures.claim: Reduced soldier damage requires target hit_count > 2, borrowing 2 from ability charges. The source reduces damage after the first soldier, including the second. The actual two-charge mechanic is not represented elsewhere.

evidence.quote: Sand Soldiers that strike the same targets deal 25% damage after the first.
This Ability has 2 charges.

failures.correction: Use a condition for subsequent soldiers striking the same target during this attack, using hit_order != first or explicit relation text rather than a charge numeral. Mark the reduced damage as replacing normal soldier damage. Add an independent ability-charge capacity rule.

failures.claim: target_type =/!= same_target encodes a relation as a target class and never states which target it is compared with. The gap claims the reference target cannot be determined even though the source names Azir's attack target.

evidence.quote: Sand Soldiers deal (20% ~ 100%)damage to enemies that are not Azir's Attack target.
Sand Soldiers that strike the same targets deal 25% damage after the first.

failures.correction: Preserve explicit text conditions: same target as the earlier soldier in this attack; or not Azir's primary attack target. Use field other if no dedicated relationship field fits. Narrow the gap to unknown interpolation, not the clearly named reference target.

failures.claim: The secondary-target percentages are recorded as min_amount/max_amount damage amounts instead of a multiplier of soldier damage.

evidence.quote: Sand Soldiers deal (20% ~ 100%)damage to enemies that are not Azir's Attack target.

failures.correction: Use damage_multiplier with both endpoints and shape level_range, retaining replaces_base. Do not infer intermediate percentages or encode the percentage endpoints as absolute damage.

failures.claim: The distance condition belongs to enemy; the source tests whether the Sand Soldier is near an enemy turret.

evidence.quote: Sand Soldiers expire twice as fast when near an enemy turret.

failures.correction: Make summon the subject of the proximity condition and keep the enemy turret as the relation target in text.

failures.claim: The candidate describes soldier damage when Azir attacks but omits that the soldier stab replaces his basic attack in soldier range.

evidence.quote: replacing his basic attack against targets within the soldier's range
When Azir Attacks an enemy near a Sand Soldier, he instead orders the soldiers to stab

failures.correction: Preserve the replacement in effect text or an attack_modifier effect. Do not imply the soldier damage is an extra normal Azir attack.

failures.claim: Meeps are required to be present, but no rule or description consumes a Meep when the enhanced attack occurs.

evidence.quote: Bard's Attacks consume a Meep to deal an additional

failures.correction: Add a resource_change effect or explicit consumption text for the same attack; apply it once to the attack, not once per affected enemy.

failures.claim: The candidate correctly follows the English buff duration, but omits the Korean wording conflict: English gives the buff for 20 seconds while out of combat; Korean describes being out of combat for 20 seconds as the condition.

evidence.quote: gaining 24% Move Speed (stacking up to 10 times) while out of combat for 20 seconds
20초 동안 전투에서 벗어나 있으면 이동 속도가 24% 증가합니다.

failures.correction: Keep the English duration interpretation and add source_conflict with both exact excerpts. Do not change the effect to a 20-second waiting requirement.

failures.claim: The candidate requires more than the necessary Chime count (gt), excluding the count that is enough.

evidence.quote: When Bard has collected enough Chimes

failures.correction: Use a text condition for having collected enough Chimes, or gte against the unresolved required threshold. Retain the unresolved-number/condition gap.

failures.claim: Random map appearance of Chimes is omitted from the summary and rules; only collection is represented.

evidence.quote: Bard attracts Chimes randomly around the map.

failures.correction: Preserve random Chime appearance around the map as text in a passive summon/other effect without inventing a spawn schedule or locations.

failures.claim: hit_order <= first restricts damage to the first enemy; target.hit_count <= 2 is a target hit count, not the first two different enemies in projectile order.

evidence.quote: magic damage to the first two enemies hit.

failures.correction: Represent first and second enemy targets explicitly, using hit order text or separate first/second target rules. Remove target hit_count as a substitute for projectile target order.

failures.claim: The stun condition is target hit_count = 2, which means a target receives two hits rather than the bolt reaching a second enemy. The effect subject does not identify both affected enemies.

evidence.quote: If the bolt hits a second enemy or a wall, any enemies hit are Stunned
if it strikes another enemy, it will stun them both.

failures.correction: Require the bolt to hit another enemy after the first and identify the first and second enemies as stun recipients. Preserve the rank-based duration.

failures.claim: There is no wall-collision stun rule. The gap treats initial target versus any enemies hit as an unresolved disagreement, although these are compatible for a wall reached after the initial enemy.

evidence.quote: If it strikes a wall, it will stun the initial target
If the bolt hits a second enemy or a wall, any enemies hit are Stunned

failures.correction: Add the wall-after-first-enemy branch that stuns the enemy already hit. Remove the unsupported disagreement claim; a text collision condition is available even without a dedicated wall enum.

failures.claim: The candidate heals on an expiry event after five seconds, with no ally entry or first-ally restriction. Five seconds is shrine maturation time, not a healing duration or automatic-heal timer.

evidence.quote: The shrine grows to restore (50/87.5/125/162.5/200 + (70% Ability Power)) Health after existing for 5 seconds.
Health to the first ally to enter.

failures.correction: Trigger mature healing when the first ally enters a shrine whose age is at least five seconds. Keep five seconds only as a shrine-age condition. Preserve the smaller heal as the minimum bound or an immature-entry case, without two unconditional healing applications.

failures.claim: The source gives 6% per 100 AP. The candidate records a 6% AP coefficient plus an amount=100 parameter, losing the denominator and suggesting a different calculation.

evidence.quote: (20/22.5/25/27.5/30% + (6% per 100 Ability Power)) Move Speed

failures.correction: Keep the per-100 relationship explicitly. Use ratio_input/ratio_output or text plus a truthful unsupported_formula gap if needed; never encode the denominator as a separate flat amount.

failures.claim: The candidate omits that a shrine disappears after healing and speeding up the first ally, allowing a shrine to appear reusable.

evidence.quote: disappearing after healing and speeding up the first ally that touches it.

failures.correction: Add a disappearance/consumption effect when the first ally activates the shrine. Keep enemy-entry destruction as its separate branch.

failures.claim: The three-shrine simultaneous maximum is attached as a summon count on cast; it is a storage capacity, not the number created by one cast.

evidence.quote: Bard can have up to 3 shrines at once.

failures.correction: Use storage_cap for the simultaneous maximum and keep the single shrine creation distinct from that capacity.

failures.claim: The word one in one-way is encoded as distance_units = 1. The gap even says it was excluded, contradicting the retained parameter.

evidence.quote: Bard opens a one-way portal through Terrain for 10 seconds.

failures.correction: Remove the distance parameter. Preserve one-way traversal in text. Update the gap so it truthfully describes excluding the lexical number rather than claiming exclusion while it remains.

failures.claim: The four ability uses are encoded as caster hit_count = 4. Uses/casts do not require hits; the stun belongs to the next damaging ability affecting a target.

evidence.quote: After using 4 Abilities, Annie's next damaging Ability Stuns

failures.correction: Represent prior ability casts as a resource/other text condition rather than hit_count. Separate building readiness from the next damaging ability hit that applies the stun; preserve the empowerment condition.

failures.claim: Game-start and respawn readiness is represented as UI information gated on already being ready; neither lifecycle event produces readiness.

evidence.quote: Annie begins the game and respawns with Pyromania available.

failures.correction: Preserve game start and respawn as lifecycle triggers/explicit text conditions that grant readiness. Remove the circular already-ready prerequisite; use a state/resource/other effect rather than treating this as only interface information.

failures.claim: The refund/reduction rule listens to an unrestricted target death and does not link that death to Disintegrate destroying its target.

evidence.quote: refunding the Mana cost if it destroys the target.
If the target dies, Annie refunds the Mana cost and reduces the Cooldown by 50%.

failures.correction: Tie the target death/kill to this fireball destroying the target, retaining a text relation condition if needed. Do not refund for arbitrary later target deaths.

failures.claim: The candidate retains only generic area damage; the source's cone targeting shape is missing from the Korean summary and effect text.

evidence.quote: Annie casts a blazing cone of fire, dealing damage to all enemies in the area.

failures.correction: Preserve the cone and enemies within it in text; no new schema field is necessary.

failures.claim: The once-per-shield retaliation has count = 60, reusing the first shield amount. activation=fired is also an unsupported condition and does not encode the once-per-current-shield limit.

evidence.quote: magic damage once per shield.
Annie grants an ally champion (60/95/130/165/200

failures.correction: Remove the count=60 parameter and the invented fired gate. Preserve the retaliation limit using an explicit text condition for this enemy/current shield and retain an honest representation gap if needed. Keep shield-active gating separate.

failures.claim: Tibbers gets the shield effects only when summon entity_count > 60, again reusing the first shield amount.

evidence.quote: Tibbers always gains the effects of Molten Shield when summoned.

failures.correction: Remove the invented numeric threshold. Preserve Tibbers being summoned/present as the condition and always granting the described shield effects.

failures.claim: All recipient mechanics are restricted to ally, omitting Annie herself despite the summary explicitly allowing Annie or an ally.

evidence.quote: Grants Annie or an ally a shield, a burst of Move Speed

failures.correction: Preserve both caster and allied champion recipients, including the retaliation branch for the shielded caster. The English body's ally champion wording does not establish an exclusion of self.

failures.claim: The summary preserves all three enrage causes, but the rule uses a generic transform plus an unsupported activation=fired gate. The gap asserts timing ambiguity between summary/body, even though the quoted English tooltip clearly lists the triggers and the summary simply does not discuss them.

evidence.quote: Tibbers becomes enraged when summoned, if Annie stuns an enemy champion, and if Annie dies.

failures.correction: Remove the invented fired gate. Represent the three alternative causes in separate trigger rules, or keep them in explicit condition text with a truthful typed limitation gap. Do not invent disagreement from source silence. The Korean tooltip omits the on-summon clause, which is source asymmetry rather than an explicit denial.

failures.claim: Manual Tibbers orders are recorded as cast with a spell_ready prerequisite, instead of the explicitly supported recast event.

evidence.quote: Recast: Manually issue orders to Tibbers.

failures.correction: Use trigger.event = recast and remove the invented spell_ready gate.

failures.claim: Tibbers' displayed stats are conditional on activation=fired. No supplied source makes possessing his normal stats depend on that activation state.

evidence.quote: Tibbers has: ((1150 ~ 3500) + (50% Ability Power)) Health

failures.correction: Remove the fired condition; use summon existence/presence if a condition is needed. This finding concerns the invented gate, not the openly unresolved pooled formula representation.

notes.detail: unknown damage recipient and missing damage-event timing are explicitly preserved by scope_ambiguous. Do not manufacture a damage recipient/attack schedule to resolve those gaps.

English summary/body explicitly say the soldier attack replaces Azir's attack. Korean summary has awkward broader wording about Azir and soldier attacks. Prefer English; this is relevant to the omitted replacement finding, without adding an unsupported extra attack.

Unknown experience, Meep generation interval, maximum Meep count, and Chime thresholds are marked unresolved. Do not guess them. The 6-per-5-Chimes term is retained as formula components and exact evidence; no explicit wrong interpolation formula is asserted.

The movement modifier retains 24%, count 10, and 20-second references, but its text would better preserve stacking up to a maximum rather than leaving count=10 unexplained. This is not counted as a separate false mechanic because the source evidence retains the cap.

The stat block is pooled under shape unknown and unsupported_formula, with exact original evidence. This loses useful stat-specific structure, and the schema could split it into health/armor/MR/AD effects, but the candidate does not assert a fabricated computed stat formula. The unrelated activation=fired prerequisite is a genuine error and is reported separately.

English tooltip explicitly includes enrage when summoned; Korean tooltip lists Annie stun/death but does not state that summon enrage is impossible. Keep the English fact. Omission alone does not prove a contradictory timing rule.
The text explicitly covers all hit units/structures and the stasis restrictions. A generic target subject here does not make the effect enemy-only.
Ordinary shield/dash/path damage is separate from the enemy-champion collision effects. The text preserves enemy scope and the Sand Soldier-charge result; no unsupported charge count is needed.
The forward soldier wall, enemy knockback/magic damage and five-second path block are preserved. No concrete source disagreement was found.
